passage: Classroom note, Tuesday. Before starting the clinic game, Arohi and Abhinav settled roles: Arohi would be the doctor and Abhinav the patient. They fetched a bandage and a toy stethoscope from the shelf, laid a mat as the clinic bed and put a chair as the waiting room. Only then did they begin. I did not step in. Later I told them the set-up looked very well organised. The teacher

qa.q: Which props did Arohi and Abhinav fetch from the shelf?
qa.a: They fetched a bandage and a toy stethoscope from the shelf.

qa.q: What might Arohi and Abhinav have been feeling as they set up the clinic?
qa.a: They were probably excited and cooperative, shown by settling roles and props before starting.

qa.q: What alternative could the children use if they disagree about roles, and why?
qa.a: They could take turns being the doctor, because agreeing on who plays which part means the play can begin without a fight.

qa.q: How does the teacher see the set-up?
qa.a: The teacher sees careful planning and holds back, choosing to praise the organised set-up afterwards rather than steering the play.

grounding: Two children assign roles, gather a toy stethoscope and a bandage, and set the clinic on the mat before playing, so set-up comes before play.
